We need propose a 5-step retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have a template (id 29646) that seems to deprotect TBS? Actually retro_smarts shows breaking TBS to give OH. The apply_template gave three possible precursors: each with TBS group on one of the OHs? The product is target with TBS? Wait target has no TBS; it's free OHs. The template likely is reverse: it adds TBS? The retro template: [C:2]-[OH]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si]... So forward is protection (adds TBS). Retro (our direction) removes TBS to give OH. Since target has OH, applying template gives precursors with TBS on one OH. The apply gave three precursors each with TBS on different OH positions. Choose one.

We need 5 steps total. Likely steps: 1) Protect one OH with TBS (forward). In retrosynthesis, we break TBS to get precursor with TBS. So step1: deprotect TBS (retro) -> precursor with TBS.

Then maybe Still-Gennari/HWE to form the conjugated diene chain and carboxylic acid. The target has a side chain: C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O (a trans-hexadienoic acid). This likely derived from Still-Gennari olefination of an aldehyde with phosphonate to give Z-alkene? But we have E? The chain appears E? Not sure.

We could break the double bonds via HWE to aldehyde + phosphonate. So step2: retro HWE (break C=C, form aldehyde + phosphonate). Need template for HWE. Search for functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" formed: "aldehydes"? Actually forward HWE forms C=C from aldehyde + phosphonate, breaking C-P and C-O. Retro would break C=C to give aldehyde and phosphonate. So functional_groups_broken: "C-C double bonds", formed: "aldehydes". Let's search.
